description:
Record money received against a thread and produce billed-versus-received statements.

Subcommands:
  log THREAD AMOUNT [-c CCY] [-d DATE] [-t HH:MM] [-a ACCOUNT] [-n NOTE] — record a receipt
  list [THREAD] [--since DATE] [--until DATE] [--json] — list payments
  statement [--thread T] [--since DATE] [--until DATE] [--as-of DATE] [--pdf PATH] [--json] — billed vs received, by thread and currency
  show ID [--json] — show one payment
  edit ID [--amount N] [-c CCY] [-d DATE] [-t HH:MM] [-a ACCOUNT] [-n NOTE] — change one field of a payment
  rm ID -y — permanently delete a payment

Args:
  THREAD  thread name, 'Kind/Name' or wikilink
  AMOUNT  positive decimal. Required in practice, although argparse marks it optional.
  ID      the payment's 8-character id, from `list`

Flags:
  log:
    -c, --currency CCY   ISO code (default: the thread's currency)
    -d, --date DATE      date received, YYYY-MM-DD (default today)
    -t, --time HH:MM     time received (default now)
    -a, --account NAME   account the money landed in
    -n, --note TEXT      free-text note
  list:
    --since DATE / --until DATE   inclusive window
    --json               JSON output
  statement:
    --thread T           one thread
    --since DATE / --until DATE   inclusive window
    --as-of DATE         statement date; drives aging (default today)
    --pdf PATH           write a PDF statement to PATH; requires --thread
    --json               JSON output
  show:
    --json               JSON output
  edit:
    --amount N, -c/--currency, -d/--date, -t/--time, -a/--account, -n/--note   new value for that field
  rm:
    -y, --yes            required to confirm

Examples:
  ["log", "Projects/SGB", "12500.00", "-d", "2026-09-28", "-a", "Business cheque"]
  ["statement", "--thread", "Projects/SGB", "--json"]
  ["statement", "--thread", "Projects/SGB", "--pdf", "statements/sgb.pdf"]
  ["list", "Projects/SGB", "--since", "2026-09-01"]

Notes:
  Statements ignore unbilled hours. A PDF statement needs client_name in the thread file.
  log also queues a REF: in the buffer, filed under the date received. It reaches the thread's daily log on the next `buffer flush`.
  Nothing prompts. rm is destructive and refuses to run without -y.
  Exit 1: amount missing, not positive or not a valid number; --pdf without --thread; nothing to state for the thread as of that date.
